examples.ko: 지진 이후 경보 단계가 한 단계 격상됐어요.
examples.en: After the earthquake, the alert level was raised by one step.
This town will be upgraded to a city starting next year.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 본부로 격상되면서 인원도 늘었어요.
examples.en: As our team was upgraded to a division, the staff increased too.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 관계가 동맹으로 격상된다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw news that the relationship between the two countries is being raised to an alliance.

examples.ko: 행사 규모가 커지면서 대회 등급이 격상될 예정이에요.
examples.en: As the event grows, the competition's grade is set to be raised.

examples.ko: 위기 단계가 격상되자 학교가 모두 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: When the crisis level was raised, all the schools closed.

explain: 등급, 지위, 단계, 관계가 위로 올라갈 때 쓰고, 뉴스에서 '경보 단계가 격상되다'처럼 자주 나와요. 반대말은 '격하되다'예요. 사람의 직급이 오르는 건 보통 '승진하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when a grade, status, level or relationship goes up, and it often appears in the news, as in '경보 단계가 격상되다'. Its opposite is '격하되다'. When a person moves up in rank, people usually say '승진하다'.

examples.en: He holds both the professor and institute director positions.

examples.ko: 팀장이 인사 업무까지 겸임해서 많이 바빠요.
examples.en: The team leader also handles HR duties, so he is very busy.

examples.ko: 한 사람이 두 자리를 겸임하기는 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It is not easy for one person to hold two posts at once.
The new president will also serve as chairman of the board.

examples.ko: 두 부서의 일을 겸임하는 직원이 늘었어요.
examples.en: The number of employees working in two departments at once has grown.
The CEO decided not to hold the director post at the same time.

explain: 한 사람이 원래 맡은 직책 말고 다른 직책이나 업무를 함께 맡을 때 써요. 회사, 학교, 정부 인사 소식에 자주 나와요. '겸직'도 비슷한 뜻으로 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '같이 맡다'라고 풀어서 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when one person takes on another post or duty in addition to their main one. It often appears in personnel news from companies, schools and the government. '겸직' is used with a similar meaning, and in daily talk people say '같이 맡다'.

examples.en: A rank badge is attached to the shoulder of the uniform.
My father polished his rank badge until it shone.
This badge means the rank of sergeant.
Let's talk comfortably today without pulling rank.
Rank badges are attached to police uniforms too.
Judging by the badges, he is the highest in rank.

explain: 군복이나 경찰·소방 제복에 달아서 계급을 나타내는 표예요. 비유로 '계급장 떼고'라고 하면 직급이나 나이를 따지지 않는다는 뜻으로 써요.

phrases.example: 오늘은 계급장 떼고 솔직하게 말해 봐요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직급이나 나이 같은 위아래 관계를 접어 두고 대등하게 이야기하자고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when proposing to set aside hierarchy such as job title or age and talk as equals.
phrases.en_equiv: drop the titles and speak as equals

explain_en: It is a badge worn on military, police or fire-service uniforms to show rank. Figuratively, '계급장 떼고' means setting aside rank or age and speaking as equals.

examples.en: He ended up rising to a senior government post.
Senior civil servants must disclose their assets.

examples.ko: 고위직에 있는 사람일수록 말을 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: The higher someone's position, the more careful they must be with their words.
My uncle works in a senior position at a bank.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 여성 고위직이 많지 않아요.
examples.en: This company doesn't have many women in senior positions.
The senior appointments were announced this morning.

explain: '고위직'은 회사나 정부의 높은 자리를 통틀어 부를 때 쓰고 뉴스에 자주 나와요. 구체적인 자리는 '장관', '임원'처럼 따로 이름이 있고 고위직은 그런 자리들의 묶음 이름이에요. 반대는 '하위직'이에요.
explain_en: 고위직 is a collective name for high positions in companies or the government, and it appears often in the news. Specific posts have their own names like 장관 and 임원, and 고위직 groups them together. The opposite is 하위직.

en: oversee; supervise; be in charge of

examples.en: This department oversees the school events.
City Hall is in charge of the city's traffic.
The director oversees the entire hospital.
Do you know who is in charge of this?

examples.ko: 한 사람이 모든 업무를 관장하기는 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard for one person to oversee all the work.
That committee was in charge of writing the exam.

explain: 기관이나 높은 자리의 사람이 어떤 일을 책임지고 맡을 때 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. '담당하다'는 실무를 맡는 느낌이고, '관장하다'는 전체를 총괄하는 느낌이에요. 뉴스와 공문에서 주로 보고, 일상 대화에서는 '맡다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is a formal word used when an organization or a person in a high position takes responsibility for a whole area of work. 담당하다 feels like handling the practical tasks, while 관장하다 feels like overseeing everything. You mostly see it in news and official documents; in daily talk people say 맡다.

examples.en: The coach used the rookie as a starter.

examples.ko: 새 대표는 젊은 인재를 적극적으로 기용하고 있어요.
examples.en: The new CEO is actively appointing young talent.

examples.ko: 회사에서 외부 전문가를 팀장으로 기용하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The company decided to appoint an outside expert as team leader.

examples.ko: 이번 드라마는 신인 배우를 주인공으로 기용해서 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: This drama got attention by casting a newcomer in the lead role.

examples.ko: 같은 사람을 계속 기용하면 불만이 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you keep picking the same person, complaints can come up.
I wonder what standard they used to pick the person.

explain: '임명하다'는 공식 직책을 맡길 때 쓰고, '기용하다'는 선수나 배우처럼 능력을 보고 써 주는 경우에도 써요. 뉴스와 스포츠 기사에서 자주 보고, 일상 대화에서는 '쓰다'나 '뽑다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: '임명하다' is for formally giving an official post, while '기용하다' also covers choosing athletes or actors because of their ability. You see it often in news and sports articles, and in daily talk people say '쓰다' or '뽑다'.

en: be unofficially decided; be tipped (for a post)

examples.en: He has been unofficially picked as the next president.

examples.ko: 신입 사원 한 명이 해외 지사로 내정돼요.
examples.en: One new employee is being lined up for an overseas branch.
There is a rumor that a candidate has already been chosen.
An article came out saying he had been lined up as the director.
People say he will be tipped for minister.
It hasn't been decided yet, so please wait.

explain: 공식 발표 전에 속으로 먼저 정해졌을 때 써요. 사장, 감독, 장관, 후보 같은 직책이나 인사 이야기에 나와요. 발표까지 끝나서 확실해진 건 '확정되다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Use it when something has been settled behind the scenes before the official announcement. It appears with posts and personnel, such as a president, coach, minister, or candidate. Once it is announced and certain, the word is '확정되다'.

examples.en: A lawyer went to the trial on my behalf.
Someone representing the manager came to the meeting.
I submitted the documents on behalf of my father.
I can't act on behalf of the boss.

examples.ko: 대신 일해 줄 분이 팀장님을 대리했어요.
examples.en: The person who worked in their place acted for the team leader.
Please first tell me whom you represent.

explain: '대신하다'는 일반적인 말이고, '대리하다'는 회사나 법에서 다른 사람 자리에서 공식적으로 일할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '대신 해 주다'가 더 자연스러워요. 직급 '대리'와 소리가 같아서 헷갈리기 쉬워요.
explain_en: 대신하다 is the general word, while 대리하다 is for officially acting in someone's place at a company or in law. In daily talk, 대신 해 주다 sounds more natural. It sounds the same as the job rank 대리, which is easy to mix up.

examples.en: When the parent company got into trouble, its subsidiary struggled too.

examples.ko: 그 병원은 모기업의 지원을 받고 있어요.
examples.en: That hospital receives support from its parent company.
The parent company increased its investment in the subsidiary.
The club's name follows that of its parent company.
The parent company and the subsidiary use the same building.
Many people invested because they trusted the parent company.

explain: 다른 회사를 거느리고 있는 회사를 말하고, 반대로 거느림을 받는 회사는 '자회사'예요. 프로 스포츠 구단이나 병원, 학교 이야기에서도 '모기업'이라는 말이 자주 나와요. 뉴스에서는 '모회사'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is the company that owns or controls other companies, and the controlled one is called '자회사'. The word often comes up in stories about pro sports clubs, hospitals and schools too. In the news it is also called '모회사'.

en: be issued (a warning); be assigned to a post

examples.ko: 오늘 아침 서울에 폭염 경보가 발령됐어요.
examples.en: A heat wave warning was issued for Seoul this morning.
As soon as the typhoon advisory was issued, the school closed.

examples.ko: 다음 달에 저는 부산 지점으로 발령돼요.
examples.en: Next month I will be posted to the Busan branch.

examples.ko: 새 팀장으로 발령된 지 한 달이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been a month since I was appointed as the new team leader.
When a cold wave warning is issued, go out less.

examples.ko: 해외 지사로 발령될지도 모른다는 소문이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a rumor that I might be posted to an overseas office.

explain: 발령되다는 두 가지로 써요. 경보·주의보 같은 알림이 내려질 때와, 회사에서 다른 부서나 지점으로 인사 이동이 정해질 때예요. 뒤의 쓰임은 '○○로 발령되다'처럼 조사 '로'와 같이 써요.
explain_en: 발령되다 has two uses: when an alert such as a warning or advisory is issued, and when a company decides to move someone to another department or branch. The second use goes with the particle 로, as in 부산 지점으로 발령되다.

en: selection (for a role or position); being picked out

examples.ko: 신인 배우의 주연 발탁이 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: The casting of a newcomer in the lead role became a hot topic.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 국가대표 발탁을 꿈꿔 왔어요.
examples.en: That player has dreamed of being picked for the national team.
Everyone was surprised by the sudden selection.

examples.ko: 젊은 직원의 부장 발탁은 회사에서 처음이에요.
examples.en: A young employee being picked for department head is a first for the company.

examples.ko: 감독의 발탁 기준은 실력이 아니라 성실함이었어요.
examples.en: The coach's selection criterion was diligence, not skill.
I teared up when I heard the news that I was chosen.

explain: '발탁'은 많은 사람 중에서 쓸 만한 사람을 골라 특별한 자리에 올려 쓰는 일에 써요. 그냥 '선택'과 달리 고르는 쪽이 윗사람이고, 뽑힌 사람이 좋은 기회를 얻는다는 느낌이 있어요. '신인 발탁', '파격 발탁'처럼 써요.
explain_en: 발탁 is for choosing a promising person out of many and putting them in a special position. Unlike plain 선택, the chooser is in a higher position and the person picked gets a good opportunity. Typical uses are 신인 발탁 and 파격 발탁.

examples.ko: 회사는 신입 사원을 교육 성적에 따라 부서에 배속해요.
examples.en: The company places new employees in departments based on their training scores.

examples.ko: 인사팀에서 저를 이번 달부터 마케팅팀에 배속했어요.
examples.en: HR assigned me to the marketing team starting this month.

examples.ko: 신입을 어느 부서에 배속할지 아직 정하지 못했어요.
examples.en: We haven't decided yet which department to place the new hire in.

examples.ko: 신병을 각 부대에 배속하는 일은 며칠 걸려요.
examples.en: Assigning new recruits to each unit takes a few days.

examples.ko: 희망한 부서에 배속해 주셔서 정말 감사해요.
examples.en: Thank you so much for placing me in the department I wanted.

examples.ko: 새로 온 간호사들을 응급실에 배속하기로 했대요.
examples.en: I heard they decided to place the new nurses in the emergency room.

explain: '배치하다'는 사람이나 물건을 자리에 두는 일 전반에 쓰고, '배속하다'는 사람을 부서나 부대에 소속시킬 때 써요. '~에 배속하다'처럼 조사 '에'와 함께 쓰고, 말할 때는 '발령 나다'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: '배치하다' covers putting people or things in a spot in general, while '배속하다' is for attaching a person to a department or unit. It takes the particle '에' as in '~에 배속하다', and in speech people also say '발령 나다'.

examples.en: The hospital director met the patient in person.
I greeted the hospital director.
The newly arrived director has a reputation for being kind.
To see the hospital director, you must make an appointment.
The hospital director and the doctors held a meeting together.
Everyone listened quietly to the director's words.

explain: '-장'은 어떤 곳의 책임자 이름에 붙어요. 학교는 '교장', 병원은 '병원장', 회사는 '사장'처럼 곳마다 말이 달라요. 높여 부를 때는 '님'을 붙여 '병원장님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: The ending '-장' marks the head of a place, and each place has its own word: '교장' for a school, '병원장' for a hospital, '사장' for a company. To show respect add '님', as in '병원장님'.

examples.en: I assist the team leader.
The secretary assisted the president from his side.
Ten staff members assist the mayor.

examples.ko: 새 총리를 보좌하고 일을 배우고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm assisting the new prime minister and learning the job.
I came to work early to assist the mayor.
We're hiring someone to assist the CEO.

explain: 윗사람이 일을 잘하도록 곁에서 돕는다는 뜻이라서 도움을 받는 사람이 나보다 높은 자리예요. 친구를 돕는 일에는 '도와주다'를 쓰고, 이 말은 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It means helping a superior do their job well from close by, so the person helped holds a higher position. For helping a friend, use 도와주다 instead.

examples.en: The manager stepped down because of poor results.
The CEO plans to resign next month.
He decided to resign and take responsibility.
On the day he resigned, he left a letter for the staff.
The university president resigned suddenly, and the school became noisy with talk.
After resigning, he went back to his hometown.

explain: '사임하다'는 높은 직책에서 스스로 물러날 때 써요. 일반 회사를 그만두는 말은 '퇴사하다'이고, '그만두다'가 가장 일상적이에요. 윗사람이 내보내는 경우는 '해임하다'라서 누가 결정했는지가 달라요.
explain_en: '사임하다' is for stepping down from a high post by choice. Leaving an ordinary company is '퇴사하다', and '그만두다' is the everyday word. If a superior removes the person it's '해임하다', so who decides differs.

examples.en: The team leader stepped down to take responsibility.

examples.ko: 감독이 성적 때문에 사퇴할 거라는 소문이 있어요.
examples.en: There's a rumor the coach will resign over the results.

examples.ko: 그 후보는 선거 전에 사퇴하기로 했어요.
examples.en: That candidate decided to withdraw before the election.
His health got worse, so he resigned as chairman.
Calls for him to resign keep coming.

examples.ko: 반장이 갑자기 사퇴해서 반 친구들이 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The class president suddenly quit, and the classmates were surprised.

explain: '그만두다'는 어디에나 쓰지만 '사퇴하다'는 회장, 감독, 위원, 후보처럼 맡은 자리나 후보 자리를 내려놓을 때 써요. 회사를 떠나는 건 '퇴사하다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 그만두다 works almost anywhere, but 사퇴하다 is for giving up a post or candidacy, such as chairperson, coach, committee member, or candidate. Leaving a company is more naturally 퇴사하다.

en: be appointed; be selected for a post

examples.en: Department head Kim was appointed as the new team leader.
Let me introduce the person who was appointed society president.
He was unanimously chosen as the representative.

examples.ko: 새 감독이 선임되면 팀이 달라질 거예요.
examples.en: When a new coach is appointed, the team will change.
An outside expert is appointed as a committee member.
As soon as he was appointed, he started reforms.

explain: 회사나 단체에서 사람이 어떤 자리를 맡도록 정해질 때 써요. 말로는 '뽑히다', '임명되다'도 써요. '선임'은 순서가 먼저인 사람, 즉 선배라는 뜻도 있으니 문장을 잘 봐야 해요.
explain_en: Used when a person is chosen for a post in a company or organization. In speech '뽑히다' or '임명되다' also work. Note that '선임' can also mean a senior person, so read the context.

examples.en: I belong to the marketing team.

examples.ko: 이 선수는 어느 팀에 소속되어 있어요?
examples.en: Which team is this player affiliated with?

examples.ko: 두 사람은 같은 동아리에 소속되어 있었어요.
examples.en: The two of them belonged to the same club.
My department changed, so I moved my seat.

examples.ko: 학교에 소속되지 않은 강사도 참여할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Instructors not affiliated with the school can take part too.

examples.ko: 신입 직원은 다음 달에 영업부에 소속될 거예요.
examples.en: The new employee will be assigned to the sales department next month.

explain: 회사·학교·팀처럼 어딘가의 한 구성원일 때 써요. 보통 '~에 소속되어 있다'로 말해요. 일상에서는 '~에서 일해요', '~ 팀이에요'가 더 자연스럽고, 명사 '소속'을 '소속이 어디예요?'처럼 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: Use it when you are a member of a company, school, team, or similar group. It is usually said as '~에 소속되어 있다'. In daily conversation, '~에서 일해요' or '~ 팀이에요' sounds more natural, and the noun '소속' is also used, as in '소속이 어디예요?'.

examples.ko: 회사 수뇌부가 오늘 긴급 회의를 열었어요.
examples.en: The company's top executives held an emergency meeting today.
We are waiting for an announcement from the government leadership.

examples.ko: 수뇌부는 이번 계획을 바꾸지 않기로 했어요.
examples.en: The leadership decided not to change this plan.
The manager talked with the club's top management for a long time.

examples.ko: 수뇌부에 있는 사람들은 현장 사정을 잘 몰라요.
examples.en: The people in the top leadership don't know the situation on the ground well.

examples.ko: 그 조직의 수뇌부를 만나려면 약속이 필요해요.
examples.en: You need an appointment to meet that organization's leadership.

explain: 회사, 정부, 단체에서 가장 높은 자리에 있는 사람들을 하나의 집단으로 부르는 말이에요. 한 사람을 가리킬 때는 쓰지 않아요. 일상에서는 '임원진', '윗분들'이라고 하고, '수뇌부'는 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 반대로 현장은 '일선'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the people in the highest positions of a company, government or group, taken as a whole, not a single person. In daily life people say '임원진' or '윗분들', while '수뇌부' appears often in the news. The opposite side is the front line, '일선'.

en: be promoted; be upgraded (to a higher status or level)

examples.en: Our team was promoted to the first division.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 내년에 시로 승격할 예정이에요.
examples.en: This village is going to be upgraded to a city next year.

examples.ko: 작은 연구소가 국가 기관으로 승격하면 지원이 늘어요.
examples.en: If the small institute is upgraded to a national agency, support will increase.
We waited a long time for the school to be upgraded to a university.

examples.ko: 승격한 팀의 선수들이 기쁨의 눈물을 흘렸어요.
examples.en: The players of the promoted team shed tears of joy.

examples.ko: 부서가 본부로 승격하면서 사람이 더 필요해졌어요.
examples.en: As the department was upgraded to a headquarters, more people became necessary.

explain: 사람의 직급이 오를 때는 '승진하다'를 쓰고, 승격하다는 팀·부서·마을·기관·리그처럼 조직이나 등급이 한 단계 높아질 때 써요. 'A가 B로 승격하다'처럼 '(으)로'를 붙여요. 반대말은 '강등되다'예요.
explain_en: When a person moves up in rank, use '승진하다'. '승격하다' is for an organization or level going up a step, such as a team, department, town, institution or league. The pattern is 'A가 B로 승격하다'. The opposite is '강등되다'.

examples.en: If you pass the exam, you advance to the next level next month.

examples.ko: 올해는 평가 점수가 좋아서 승급 대상에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: My evaluation score was good this year, so I made the list for advancement.
When you move up a grade, your base pay rises one step.
He advanced a rank in the taekwondo belt test.
I didn't advance, so I have to wait until next year.
My colleague moved up first, so I congratulated them.

explain: 급수, 등급, 호봉처럼 '급'이 올라갈 때 써요. 직위가 올라갈 때는 '승진하다'를 쓰고, '승급'은 월급 단계나 실력 등급이 오르는 데 더 잘 맞아요. 태권도 띠나 시험 급수 이야기에도 나와요.
explain_en: Use it when a grade, level or pay step goes up. When a job position goes up, use '승진하다'; '승급' fits pay steps and skill levels better. It also appears in talk about taekwondo belts and exam levels.

examples.en: The bus driver greeted the passengers.
My father worked as a taxi driver for a long time.

examples.ko: 운전수 아저씨가 길을 잘 알고 계세요.
examples.en: The driver knows the way well.
I saw an ad looking for a truck driver.
Drivers must be careful about drowsy driving.
I heard Grandfather's house had a separate chauffeur.

explain: 직업으로 차를 모는 사람을 말하는데, '운전수'는 오래된 느낌이 있어요. 지금은 '운전기사'나 '기사님'이 더 정중해서 많이 써요. 직접 부를 때는 '기사님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It means a person who drives a vehicle as a job, but 운전수 sounds old-fashioned. Today 운전기사 or 기사님 is more polite and common. When addressing the person directly, say 기사님.

en: appoint (an outside person to a post); commission

examples.en: The city appointed that professor as a committee member.

examples.ko: 회사는 다음 달에 새 자문위원을 위촉할 거예요.
examples.en: The company will appoint a new advisor next month.

examples.ko: 대표가 분야별 전문가 세 명을 직접 위촉해요.
examples.en: The head personally appoints three experts, one for each field.
The ceremony to appoint the ambassador is held today.

examples.ko: 협회에서 저를 심사위원으로 위촉해서 정말 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was really surprised that the association appointed me as a judge.

examples.ko: 위원을 위촉하기 전에 이름을 먼저 확인해요.
examples.en: Before appointing the members, we check the names first.

explain: 공식적으로 일을 맡길 때 쓰는 말이라 친구 사이에서는 거의 안 써요. '위원으로 위촉하다'처럼 '-(으)로'와 같이 쓰고, 맡는 쪽은 '위촉되다'라고 해요. '임명하다'는 자기 조직 사람에게 직책을 주는 느낌이고, 위촉은 바깥 전문가에게 부탁해서 맡기는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: This is a formal word, so you will hardly hear it between friends. It is used with '-(으)로' as in '위원으로 위촉하다', and the person who receives the role is described with '위촉되다'. '임명하다' feels like giving a post to someone inside your own organization, while 위촉하다 feels like asking an outside expert to take the role.

examples.en: Only the president has authority over employee personnel decisions.
The person with personnel authority decides promotions.
There is controversy over the president's appointment powers.

examples.ko: 팀장은 인사권이 없어서 채용을 못 해요.
examples.en: A team leader has no hiring authority, so they can't recruit.

examples.ko: 인사권을 함부로 쓰면 직원들이 불만을 가져요.
examples.en: If you use personnel power carelessly, employees become dissatisfied.
The company's personnel authority belongs only to the CEO.

explain: 여기서 '인사'는 인사하다의 인사가 아니라 사람을 뽑고 배치하고 승진시키는 일이에요. 그런 권한을 가진 사람은 '인사권자'라고 해요. 회사나 정치 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Here '인사' is not the greeting from '인사하다'; it means hiring, assigning and promoting people. The person with that power is called '인사권자'. It appears often in business and political news.

examples.en: Manager Kim was appointed as the new team leader.

examples.ko: 그는 대사로 임명돼서 곧 외국으로 떠나요.
examples.en: He was appointed ambassador and will soon leave for abroad.

examples.ko: 새로 임명된 교장 선생님이 인사를 하셨어요.
examples.en: The newly appointed principal gave a greeting.

examples.ko: 회장으로 임명되면 책임이 더 무거워질 거예요.
examples.en: If you are appointed chairman, the responsibility will get heavier.
I wonder who will be appointed as the head.
Ministers are appointed by the president.

explain: 윗사람이나 기관이 정해서 어떤 자리를 맡게 될 때 써요. 투표로 뽑히면 '선출되다'이고, 위에서 정해 주면 '임명되다'예요. 자리를 맡기는 쪽은 '임명하다'를 써요.
explain_en: Used when a superior or an organization picks someone for a position. If people vote someone in, it's 선출되다, and if someone above chooses them, it's 임명되다. The one handing out the post uses 임명하다.

examples.en: The new team leader received the certificate of appointment today.
The name and position are written on the certificate of appointment.

examples.ko: 임명장 받는 날에는 가족이 모두 와요.
examples.en: On the day of receiving the appointment certificate, the whole family comes.

examples.ko: 이 임명장은 액자에 넣어 둘 거예요.
examples.en: I'm going to put this appointment certificate in a frame.
An appointment certificate is hanging on the office wall.
I started the work without even an appointment certificate.

explain: '임명장을 받다', '임명장을 주다'와 함께 쓰고, 행사 이름으로는 '임명장 수여식'이라고 해요. 윗사람에게 줄 때는 '임명장을 드리다'라고 높여요.
explain_en: It goes with '임명장을 받다' (receive) and '임명장을 주다' (give), and the ceremony is called '임명장 수여식'. When giving it to a superior, you say '임명장을 드리다'.

examples.ko: 그 시장은 재임 기간에 도로를 많이 넓혔어요.
examples.en: The mayor widened many roads during the term in office.

examples.ko: 재임 중에 큰 사고가 없어서 다행이에요.
examples.en: I am glad there was no major accident during the tenure.

examples.ko: 사장님이 재임하신 5년 동안 회사가 많이 커졌어요.
examples.en: The company grew a lot during the five years the president was in office.

examples.ko: 교장 선생님은 재임 시절에 학생들을 정말 아꼈어요.
examples.en: The principal really cared for the students while in office.

examples.ko: 대통령의 재임 기간은 법으로 정해져 있어요.
examples.en: The length of a president's term is set by law.

examples.ko: 재임 마지막 해에 새 건물이 완성됐어요.
examples.en: The new building was completed in the last year of the term.

explain: '재임 기간', '재임 중'처럼 써요. 자리를 맡을 때는 '취임', 그만둘 때는 '퇴임'이라서 '취임, 재임, 퇴임' 순서로 묶어 기억하면 쉬워요. 뉴스나 공식적인 글에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It appears in set phrases like 재임 기간 (term of office) and 재임 중 (while in office). Taking a post is 취임 and leaving it is 퇴임, so remember the order 취임, 재임, 퇴임. It is common in news and formal writing.

examples.en: The school reorganized its classes this year.
The company decided to reshuffle its departments.

examples.ko: 방송국이 저녁 프로그램을 재편성해서 시간이 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: The broadcaster rescheduled its evening shows, so the times changed.

examples.ko: 감독님이 선수들을 재편성하면 경기가 달라질 거예요.
examples.en: If the coach reshuffles the players, the game will change.
I heard they are reorganizing the transit routes.
The members changed, so we have to regroup the teams.

explain: 사람이나 노선, 프로그램의 구성을 한꺼번에 다시 짤 때 써요. '재정비하다'가 가다듬어 갖추는 쪽이라면 재편성하다는 구성 자체를 바꾸는 쪽이에요. 조나 반을 나눌 때는 '다시 나누다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: Use it when you rebuild the setup of people, routes or programs all at once. While '재정비하다' leans toward tidying and equipping, 재편성하다 changes the composition itself. For dividing groups or classes, people also say '다시 나누다'.

examples.en: I'm being transferred to the Busan branch next month.

examples.ko: 아이 학교 때문에 가족이 먼저 다른 도시로 전출했어요.
examples.en: Because of the kid's school, the family moved out to another city first.
I heard my colleague is transferring from headquarters to the research center.

examples.ko: 주소를 옮기면 원래 살던 곳에서 전출하고 새로 전입 신고를 해야 해요.
examples.en: When you change your address, you have to move out of your old place and register at the new one.

examples.ko: 전출하기 전에 인수인계를 꼼꼼히 해 주세요.
examples.en: Please hand over your work carefully before you transfer.

examples.ko: 직원이 한꺼번에 전출하면 남은 사람들이 힘들어요.
examples.en: If many employees transfer out at once, the people who remain have a hard time.

explain: 사람이 소속이나 주소를 옮겨 나갈 때 써요. 받는 쪽에서는 '전입하다'라고 해요. 회사 안에서는 '발령이 나다', '옮기다'라고 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is used when a person leaves one workplace or address for another. From the receiving side, you say '전입하다'. Inside a company, people also say '발령이 나다' or '옮기다'.

examples.ko: 정년퇴직을 앞둔 선배가 후배들에게 점심을 샀어요.
examples.en: A senior colleague about to retire bought lunch for the juniors.
My father retires at the mandatory age next year.
When I retire, I want to farm in the countryside.
Everyone was sad to hear our teacher is retiring.

examples.ko: 정년퇴직한 뒤에 여행을 많이 다니고 계세요.
examples.en: Since retiring, he has been traveling a lot.
At my company you have to retire at age 60.

explain: 정해진 나이가 되어 일을 그만두는 것을 말해요. 회사를 그만두는 '퇴사하다'와 달라요. 윗사람 이야기를 할 때는 '정년퇴직하시다'로 높여요.
explain_en: It means leaving work upon reaching the set retirement age, which differs from '퇴사하다' (quit a company). For a respected person, use the honorific '정년퇴직하시다'.

examples.en: A new club was formed.
This group is made up of students.
It's a well-organized team, so work is quick.
A committee will be formed for the event.
The residents gathered, and a village group was formed.
The team hasn't been properly organized yet.

explain: 사람들이 모여서 역할을 나누고 하나의 단체가 만들어질 때 써요. '단체가 조직되다'처럼 단체가 주어예요. 만드는 사람이 주어이면 '조직하다'예요. '구성되다'는 어떤 부분으로 이루어졌는지에 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: Used when people gather, split roles and a group takes shape, so the group is the subject. If the founder is the subject, the active form is used. A near neighbor, 'be composed', focuses more on which parts make up the whole.

examples.en: The CEO nominated Manager Kim as team leader.
The teacher called on me, so I answered in front of the class.
Who will you nominate at the next meeting?

examples.ko: 사회자가 손을 든 학생을 지명하고 질문을 받았어요.
examples.en: The host picked a student with a raised hand and took the question.

examples.ko: 감독이 새 주장을 지명하는 순간 모두 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: The moment the coach named the new captain, everyone applauded.
The candidate I nominated was elected in the end.

explain: 공식적인 자리에서 사람을 골라 일을 맡기거나 발표를 시킬 때 써요. 친구끼리는 '고르다', '찍다'를 더 많이 말해요. '~을/를 ~(으)로 지명하다' 형태로 써요.
explain_en: Use it in formal settings when you pick someone for a role or call on them to speak. Among friends people say '고르다' or '찍다' more often. The pattern is '~을/를 ~(으)로 지명하다'.

examples.en: The general director of this performance is a famous stage director.
The head director checked the rehearsal personally.
I'm nervous because I took on the role of general director of the opening ceremony.

examples.ko: 영화 속 장면은 총감독의 생각대로 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: The scenes in the film were changed according to the head director's idea.
I wrote an email to pass my opinion to the general director.
Who is the general director of the Olympic opening ceremony?

explain: '총감독'은 여러 감독과 담당자를 모두 이끄는 가장 높은 감독이에요. 영화나 드라마는 '감독', 큰 행사나 공연은 팀이 많아서 '총감독'을 따로 두어요. 이름 뒤에는 '총감독님'처럼 '님'을 붙여 존중해요.
explain_en: 총감독 is the top director who leads all other directors and staff. A film or drama has a 감독, while a large event or show has many teams and so a separate 총감독. After a name, add 님, as in 총감독님, to show respect.

en: oversee; sum up as a whole

examples.en: Manager Kim oversees this event.
Who is the person in charge of the whole project?

examples.ko: 저는 올해부터 마케팅 팀을 총괄하게 되었어요.
examples.en: From this year I came to lead the marketing team.

examples.ko: 모든 일정을 한 사람이 총괄하면 편해요.
examples.en: It's convenient when one person manages the whole schedule.

examples.ko: 회의가 끝나고 팀장님이 내용을 총괄해서 말해 줬어요.
examples.en: After the meeting, the team leader summed up the content.

examples.ko: 이 일을 누가 총괄할지 아직 안 정했어요.
examples.en: We haven't decided yet who will be in charge of this.

explain: 여러 부분을 한데 모아 책임지고 이끄는 일에 써요. '관리하다'는 맡은 것을 돌보는 것이고, '총괄하다'는 전체를 책임지는 느낌이에요. '총괄 책임자'처럼 앞에 붙여 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is for taking charge of many parts together and leading them. '관리하다' is looking after what you're assigned, but '총괄하다' carries the sense of being responsible for the whole. It can also be placed in front of a noun, as in '총괄 책임자'.

examples.en: The new president took office this morning.

examples.ko: 다음 달에 새 교장 선생님이 취임할 거예요.
examples.en: A new principal will take up the post next month.
On the day he took office, he greeted the staff.
The newly installed mayor met with citizens.
The company has changed a lot since he took over.
She became the president of the academic society last month.

explain: 사장, 교장, 시장처럼 높은 자리를 처음 맡을 때 써요. 일반 직원으로 회사에 들어가는 건 '입사하다'예요. 반대로 그 자리에서 물러날 때는 '퇴임하다'나 '사임하다'를 써요.
explain_en: Use it when someone takes a high-level post for the first time, such as a company president, principal, or mayor. Joining a company as a regular employee is 입사하다. Leaving the post is 퇴임하다 or 사임하다.

examples.en: My father is a white-collar worker who works in an office.
White-collar workers mostly work at desks.
I researched the pay gap between white-collar and blue-collar workers.
A white-collar worker's day usually starts with a meeting.
He went to college to become a white-collar worker.

examples.ko: 화이트칼라라도 현장에 나가야 할 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Even white-collar workers sometimes have to go out into the field.

explain: 영어 white-collar에서 온 말로 사무실에서 일하는 사무직·전문직을 가리켜요. 몸을 쓰는 일을 하는 '블루칼라'와 짝으로 자주 나와요. 일상에서는 그냥 '사무직'이라고도 많이 해요.
explain_en: Borrowed from English 'white-collar', it refers to office and professional workers. It often pairs with '블루칼라' for manual labor. In everyday speech people also simply say '사무직'.

examples.en: The street cleaner sweeps the road from early dawn.
I greet the sanitation worker every morning.
I saw a sanitation worker collecting the trash.
Thanks to the sanitation workers, the streets are always clean.
My father worked as a sanitation worker for twenty years.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에도 환경미화원들이 일하고 있었어요.
examples.en: Even on a rainy day, the sanitation workers were out working.

explain: 거리나 건물을 청소하고 쓰레기를 치우는 분을 정중하게 부르는 말이에요. '청소부'보다 존중하는 느낌이라 공식적인 자리나 뉴스에서 많이 써요.
explain_en: This is a polite term for people who clean streets and buildings and collect trash. It sounds more respectful than '청소부', so it is used in formal settings and in the news.
